test_title: SSC Stenographer 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 10 Dec, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive speech.

The secretary has planted a lot of saplings to save the environment.

options.text: A lot of saplings are being planted by the secretary to save the environment.
A lot of saplings are planted by the secretary to save the environment.
A lot of saplings were planted by the secretary to save the environment.
A lot of saplings have been planted by the secretary to save the environment.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "The secretary has planted a lot of saplings to save the environment."
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object "a lot of saplings" at the beginning.
 
• Change the active verb form "has planted" to "have been planted" (present perfect passive).
 
• Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "the secretary."
 
• Ensure the purpose phrase "to save the environment" remains at the end of the sentence for clarity.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"A lot of saplings have been planted by the secretary to save the environment."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **"A lot of saplings are being planted by the secretary to save the environment." – Incorrect tense (present continuous passive).
 
• **Option 2: **"A lot of saplings are planted by the secretary to save the environment." – Incorrect tense (simple present passive).
 
• **Option 3: **"A lot of saplings were planted by the secretary to save the environment." – Incorrect tense (simple past passive).
